reconstructed_theorem: For every real Hilbert space E (a complete real inner product space, with no finite-dimensional restriction), every function f:E→ℝ, and all real constants α, β, h, assume f is globally continuously Fréchet differentiable; for every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+t y) ≤ (1−t)f(x)+t f(y)−(α/2)t(1−t)‖y−x‖²; h≥0; βh≤1; and for every x,y∈E, f(y) ≤ f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+(β/2)‖y−x‖². Here ∇f(x) is the actual Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative of f at x, and define T(x)=x−h∇f(x). Then for every x,z∈E, ‖T(x)−z‖²+2h(f(T(x))−f(z)) ≤ (1−αh)‖x−z‖².
semantic_notes: All parameters and the space are universally quantified; all hypotheses are global. The comparator z is arbitrary and is not required to minimize f.
The gradient is derived from f; no supplied vector field, supplied derivative, or externally specified sequence is assumed.
Neither α≥0 nor β≥0 nor h>0 is assumed. The chord condition explicitly allows a real, possibly negative α. There is no αh≤1 hypothesis in this packet.
The upper quadratic inequality is itself assumed; there is no separately stated Lipschitz-gradient hypothesis.
The function-value difference is f(T(x))−f(z), with a positive coefficient 2h on the left. No nonnegativity of this difference is assumed.
At h=0, T(x)=x and the conclusion reduces to ‖x−z‖²≤‖x−z‖². There is no iteration index in this theorem.

reconstructed_theorem: For every real Hilbert space E (a complete real inner product space, with no finite-dimensional restriction), every function f:E→ℝ, and all real constants α, β, h, assume f is globally continuously Fréchet differentiable; for every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+t y) ≤ (1−t)f(x)+t f(y)−(α/2)t(1−t)‖y−x‖²; h≥0; βh≤1; and for every x,y∈E, f(y) ≤ f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+(β/2)‖y−x‖². Here ∇f(x) is the actual Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative of f at x, and define T(x)=x−h∇f(x). Assume additionally αh≤1, and write q=1−αh, so q≥0. Then for every x₀,z∈E and every natural number N≥0, with x_N=T^[N](x₀) denoting exactly N repetitions of T, (2h ∑_{k=0}^{N−1} q^k)(f(x_N)−f(z)) ≤ q^N ‖x₀−z‖². The empty sum for N=0 is zero, T^[0] is the identity, and q^0=1 even when q=0.
semantic_notes: The iterates are actual repeated applications of x↦x−h∇f(x), with ∇f the Riesz vector of the actual derivative; no free or supplied iteration sequence appears.
The comparator z is universally quantified and need not be an optimizer, stationary point, or point satisfying a function-value ordering.
The additional αh≤1 ensures q≥0, but no α≥0, β≥0, or strict h>0 hypothesis appears. In particular q is not explicitly bounded above by 1.

The finite geometric sum has N terms with exponents 0 through N−1 and multiplies the single last-iterate value difference f(x_N)−f(z); it is not a weighted sum of function values along the trajectory.
The bound retains the geometric sum without division, so α=0, h=0, q=0, and N=0 are all included. For α=0, q=1 and the sum is N. For h=0 the left side is zero.
For N=0 the conclusion is 0≤‖x₀−z‖². For q=0 and N≥1 the sum equals 1 and q^N=0. No positive denominator or positivity of the function-value difference is assumed.
The right side has exponent N, not N−1, and no final distance term remains on the left.
